extracted.name: Buttermilk Bread
extracted.description: This recipe yields two loaves of white buttermilk bread, a deservedly popular bread.
ingredient_lines: 0.5 cup warm water (110 degrees F/45 degrees C)
instruction_lines: Sprinkle yeast over warm water in a small bowl; let stand until foamy, about 5 minutes.
Place butter or margarine and buttermilk in a small saucepan. Heat slowly until the butter or margarine melts; cool to lukewarm.

Place sugar, salt, baking soda, buttermilk mixture, and yeast in large mixing bowl. Add 3 cups flour one cup at a time, and mix with the dough hook attachment of an electric mixer. Gradually add the remaining flour while continuing to mix. When dough is not sticky, turn out on a lightly floured surface. Knead for several minutes, until the dough is soft and smooth. Place in a greased bowl, and turn once. Allow to rise until doubled in size.
Punch down the dough; divide and shape into 2 loaves. Place loaves into two well-greased 8x4-inch loaf pans. Let rise until dough is 1 inch above the tops of the pans.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Bake in the preheated oven until loaves are golden brown and sound hollow when tapped on the bottom, 30 to 35 minutes.
